question: What is the primary goal of problem solving in nursing practice?

options.A: To delay vital patient care until doctors arrive
options.B: To reduce the number of shifts a nurse has to work
options.C: To replace the standard hospital administrative rules
options.D: To identify issues and ensure safe patient outcomes

explanation: Problem solving focuses on recognizing clinical issues quickly and taking action to keep patients safe. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T7#GNS112_U3_T7_h1)

question: A parole patient misses two clinic appointments in a row. What should the mental health team do?

options.A: Wait patiently until the patient decides to call the clinic back.
options.B: Check in on the patient quickly to see if they are relapsing.
options.C: Assume the patient is doing wonderfully and needs no contact.
options.D: Discharge the patient from the program for breaking the rules.

explanation: That's right! Missing appointments is an early warning sign that symptoms might be worsening or the patient is slipping away from treatment.

question: What does a psychologically safe nursing classroom help students do?

options.A: Ignore hospital safety guidelines during patient care
options.B: Pass all nursing board examinations without studying
options.C: Skip difficult clinical shifts without facing any penalties
options.D: Admit what they do not know without fear of harsh judgment

explanation: When you feel safe, you can freely speak up about mistakes or confusion without being judged. That openness is key to keeping patients safe in the clinic!

question: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of descriptive research?

options.A: Generating useful baseline data for future studies
options.B: Providing a clear picture of health habits in a community
options.C: Proving definitively which nursing intervention cures chronic illness
options.D: Being relatively fast and cost-effective to carry out

explanation: Descriptive research is great for painting a picture or saving time and money, but proving a cure requires heavy-duty experimental trials! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h7)

question: Why must a woman with an intact uterus take progesterone along with estrogen replacement therapy?

options.A: To stop the ovaries from producing any remaining androgens
options.B: To eliminate the risk of developing hot flashes
options.C: To prevent the development of high blood pressure
options.D: To prevent the buildup of the uterine lining and lower the risk of cancer

explanation: Estrogen alone can cause the uterine lining to grow too thick, raising cancer risks. Adding progesterone keeps the lining safe and balanced!

question: What three major sciences are combined in nursing informatics?

options.A: Nursing, computer, and information science
options.B: Medicine, engineering, and data science
options.C: Biology, statistics, and administrative science
options.D: Pharmacy, technology, and social science

explanation: Nursing informatics merges nursing practice with computer and information sciences to manage patient data effectively. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T2#GNS113_U1_T2_h1)

question: At what angle should you give a standard subcutaneous (SC) injection?

options.A: 90 degrees
options.B: 180 degrees
options.C: 45 degrees
options.D: 15 degrees

explanation: A 45-degree angle places the vaccine right into the fatty layer just beneath the skin where it belongs.

question: What is the purpose of food security early warning systems?

options.A: To predict exact rainfall amounts for the next ten years
options.B: To stop international trade negotiations permanently
options.C: To warn citizens about high prices in luxury restaurants
options.D: To detect impending food shortages before famine strikes

explanation: Early warning systems monitor data so authorities can respond before a crisis becomes a full-scale famine. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h7)

question: A nurse, a pharmacist, and a ward manager need to discuss a complex treatment plan for a critical patient. Which meeting format should they use?

options.A: Hospital board meeting
options.B: Administrative budget briefing
options.C: Multidisciplinary case conference
options.D: General staff handover

explanation: When different health professionals team up for a tricky patient case, it's called a multidisciplinary case conference.

question: A relative panics after noticing strange, irregular breathing patterns in a dying patient. How do you respond?

options.A: Confirm that the patient is in severe, unmanaged pain
options.B: Immediately start emergency cardiopulmonary resuscitation
options.C: Tell the relative to leave the room until breathing normalizes
options.D: Explain that changing breathing patterns are a normal part of dying

explanation: Giving a calm heads-up about changes like Cheyne-Stokes breathing helps soothe the family's fears during those final hours.

question: Why do quantitative researchers try to remain completely neutral and detached from their study participants?

options.A: To avoid having to write detailed nursing care plans
options.B: To prevent personal bias from affecting the study results
options.C: To make it easier to recruit busy hospital staff
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of running the project

explanation: Staying objective ensures the data truly reflects reality, rather than what the researcher hopes or wishes to see.

question: Who are peer champions in the context of sustaining ward improvements?

options.A: Hospital security officers who check building entry badges
options.B: Senior pharmacists who manage drug storage and inventory
options.C: Respected staff nurses who mentor newcomers and keep protocols alive
options.D: External consultants hired from foreign countries for yearly audits

explanation: Peer champions are vital because they guide junior colleagues and maintain standards long after formal project trainers leave. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is the safest way for a new mother to clean her perineal area after using the toilet?

options.A: Soaking in soapy bathwater
options.B: Washing from back to front
options.C: Washing from front to back
options.D: Wiping vigorously with dry paper

explanation: Front to back always! This golden rule keeps germs from the anal area away from the vagina and urethra, protecting her from nasty infections.

question: How can a nurse prevent reading errors (parallax errors) when using a weighing scale?

options.A: Reading the scale directly at eye level
options.B: Using a digital scale instead of an analog one
options.C: Weighing the child twice and taking the average
options.D: Calibrating the scale with a known standard weight

explanation: Looking at the dial or screen from above or the side can skew your reading. Always position your eyes straight in front of the display!

question: What happens as a normal body reflex when a patient is given a direct-acting vasodilator?

options.A: Profound bradycardia
options.B: Severe bronchial spasm
options.C: Reflex tachycardia
options.D: Significant hypokalemia

explanation: Spot on! When blood pressure drops suddenly from a vasodilator, your nervous system panics a bit and speeds up the heart to compensate.

question: Why is growing different types of crops (crop diversity) on small farms good for community nutrition?

options.A: It stops pests from destroying the main staple crop
options.B: It prevents seasonal vitamin deficiencies by providing varied nutrients
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for agricultural irrigation
options.D: It ensures that farmers only grow what sells for the highest profit

explanation: When farms grow a variety of crops, people get different vitamins and nutrients, which stops specific deficiency diseases. Brilliant concept to remember!

question: What is the primary cause of hypovolemic shock?

options.A: Sudden pump failure of the heart muscle
options.B: Physical blockage of blood flow in the lungs
options.C: Widespread widening of blood vessels from infection
options.D: Severe loss of circulating blood or fluid volume

explanation: Hypovolemia literally means low volume, caused by bleeding, burns, or severe fluid depletion. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T5#GNS123_U3_T5_h3)

question: How do hard scars (plaques) cause symptoms in disseminated sclerosis?

options.A: They cause excess production of spinal fluid in the brain ventricles
options.B: They stimulate muscles to contract constantly without rest
options.C: They repair the damaged nerves completely back to normal
options.D: They block and slow down electrical signals traveling along nerve fibers

explanation: When inflammation creates scar tissue (plaques), it gets in the way of smooth electrical conduction—leading to the physical and sensory changes patients feel.

question: Which hormone is mainly responsible for triggering the milk 'let-down' reflex when breastfeeding?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Progesterone
options.C: Estrogen
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Wonderful! Oxytocin makes tiny muscles around the milk glands squeeze, pushing the milk forward for the baby. It's also the hormone of love and bonding!

question: Why is personal willpower alone often not enough to ensure a healthy diet for poor patients?

options.A: Healthy foods do not provide enough energy for daily work
options.B: Poor individuals lack the physical ability to digest healthy foods
options.C: Low-income individuals usually prefer the taste of processed foods
options.D: Financial and environmental barriers heavily restrict their food choices

explanation: Even when people want to eat healthy, poverty and a lack of nearby resources can make it really tough to access fresh, nutritious food. You've got this!

question: A 17-year-old girl is worried she will forget to take a daily pill. Which contraceptive option fits her lifestyle best?

options.A: Subdermal contraceptive implant
options.B: Periodic calendar rhythm tracking
options.C: Standard male latex condoms
options.D: Combined oral contraceptive pills

explanation: Implants offer long-term protection without needing daily attention, making them great for busy students.

question: What is the primary purpose of irrigating a fresh wound with normal saline?

options.A: To wash away bacteria and loose debris
options.B: To numb the pain temporarily
options.C: To close the skin edges tightly
options.D: To stop bleeding from large arteries

explanation: High-volume fluid irrigation physically flushes out contaminants that could otherwise cause a localized infection. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is a great natural food source of folic acid?

options.A: Refined white sugar
options.B: Pasteurized whole milk
options.C: Green leafy vegetables
options.D: Processed red meat

explanation: Green leafy veggies like ugu, spinach, and bitter leaf are absolute powerhouses for natural folate. Eat your greens!

question: A massive movement of young people from rural farming villages into a crowded capital city is an example of which demographic process?

options.A: High fertility
options.B: Child mortality
options.C: Population capping
options.D: Internal migration

explanation: When people move from one place to another within the same country—like leaving the village for the city—we call it internal migration.

question: If a pain-relief trial shows patients actually felt *more* distressed after the new method, what should the discussion do?

options.A: Conclude that the nursing profession should stop measuring pain entirely
options.B: Change the data labels so distress looks like pain relief
options.C: Examine what factors might have caused this surprising increase in distress
options.D: Publish the paper immediately without mentioning the pain scores

explanation: Spot on! We can't hide unexpected outcomes. Facing them head-on helps protect patients and improves future care.

question: Up to how many weeks of pregnancy is an abortion generally defined to occur?

options.A: Under 20 to 22 weeks of gestation
options.B: Any time after 40 weeks of gestation
options.C: At exactly 28 weeks of gestation
options.D: Between 32 and 36 weeks of gestation

explanation: We define an abortion as the end of a pregnancy before the baby can survive outside the womb, which is generally under 20 to 22 weeks. You've got this!

question: Why shouldn't you squeeze a manual resuscitator bag way too hard during ventilation?

options.A: It causes the oxygen tank to explode
options.B: It instantly damages the heart muscle
options.C: It prevents carbon dioxide from leaving the room
options.D: It can force air into the stomach and cause vomiting

explanation: Squeezing too hard opens up the pathway to the stomach. Filling the stomach with air is a quick ticket to vomiting and aspiration—definitely something we want to avoid!

question: Which muscle groups need the most strengthening when a patient is learning to use crutches after an amputation?

options.A: Facial and neck muscles
options.B: Small toe flexors
options.C: Lower leg calf muscles
options.D: Upper body and core muscles

explanation: Using crutches without a lower limb means the arms, shoulders, and chest have to do all the heavy lifting. Time for some push-ups!

question: A patient struggles with English, and her young son offers to translate for you. What is the best thing to do?

options.A: Use hand gestures instead of words to avoid needing any translation.
options.B: Accept the son's help immediately to save time on the ward.
options.C: Ask another nurse who is busy with medication to translate.
options.D: Request a certified medical interpreter to ensure accurate translation.

explanation: Correct! Certified interpreters keep things confidential and medically accurate, whereas family members might leave out important details.

question: What is the most immediate danger when someone has severe, nonstop vomiting and diarrhea?

options.A: Upper airway obstruction
options.B: Chronic hair loss
options.C: Severe dehydration
options.D: Permanent hearing impairment

explanation: Losing water and electrolytes too fast causes blood pressure to crash, which can quickly become life-threatening if not treated.

question: What happens during passive health surveillance?

options.A: The government bans the collection of all health statistics
options.B: Nurses actively hunt for sick people in every single household
options.C: Patients diagnose themselves at home without telling anyone
options.D: Clinics routinely report disease cases upward to health authorities

explanation: In passive surveillance, we wait for patients to come to the clinic feeling unwell, and then our routine reports flow up to the health authorities. It's the standard way we track everyday illnesses!

question: Why must an unconscious patient be turned to their side when you are cleaning their mouth?

options.A: To prevent liquids from entering the airway and causing choking
options.B: To stop them from rolling off the bed
options.C: To increase blood flow to the facial nerves
options.D: To make it easier to brush the back teeth

explanation: Awesome! Turning them to the side lets water and saliva pool in the cheek and run out safely, rather than choking their airway.

question: You are putting AED pads on a man with a very hairy chest, and the pads won't stick well. What should you do right away?

options.A: Press the pads down firmly over the thick hair anyway
options.B: Skip using the AED and rely entirely on chest compressions
options.C: Apply conductive ultrasound gel over the dry hair first
options.D: Shave the hair quickly using a razor from the AED kit

explanation: Hair creates air pockets that block the electrical current. Luckily, AED kits come with a handy little razor so you can do a quick dry shave and get a solid stick!

question: Why must a nurse flush a feeding tube before and after giving medication or formula?

options.A: To cool down the internal stomach lining
options.B: To stimulate natural saliva production
options.C: To prevent the tube from clogging
options.D: To increase the patient's daily water weight

explanation: Feeding tubes are narrow and can easily block up with thick formula or crushed meds. A simple water flush keeps everything flowing smoothly.

question: Why do babies born to teenage mothers face higher risks of developmental delays?

options.A: Complete absence of breast milk production in teenagers
options.B: Mandatory separation of mother and child at birth
options.C: A combination of physical prematurity and the mother's limited caregiving maturity
options.D: Automatic genetic mutations caused by young maternal age

explanation: You got it! Being born early plays a part, and young mothers may also need extra guidance on caring for a baby as they grow.

question: What happens when a normal proto-oncogene gets mutated?

options.A: It turns into an oncogene that drives nonstop cell division
options.B: It immediately forces the cell to undergo programmed death
options.C: It repairs all surrounding damaged DNA strands instantly
options.D: It stops all cellular activity and puts the cell to sleep

explanation: Proto-oncogenes are like the gas pedal for cell growth. When mutated, they become oncogenes that push the pedal all the way down!

question: You are getting a ventilated, unstable patient ready for a CT scan. What is your most important safety check?

options.A: Turning off all continuous intravenous drug infusions to save battery life
options.B: Ensuring portable oxygen, monitor, and emergency equipment are fully functional
options.C: Removing all patient identification bands to prevent scanning delays
options.D: Notifying the hospital cafeteria that the patient will miss lunch

explanation: Always make sure your transport life support gear is fully charged and working so you are ready for anything while away from the ICU.

question: Why do community health nurses conduct a situation analysis before starting a new project?

options.A: To immediately distribute free medications to every household
options.B: To replace the national health budget with local funds
options.C: To punish local clinics for poor performance records
options.D: To understand community health status and resources before planning

explanation: Think of a situation analysis as your baseline check! You always want to understand what's currently happening and what resources are available before jumping in to plan care.

question: Why do nurses working in disaster zones need to understand how search and rescue operations work?

options.A: Healthcare delivery often starts right at the edge of the rescue zone
options.B: Nurses are required to operate heavy machinery during building collapses
options.C: Medical staff must personally enter unstable structures to find victims
options.D: Hospital administrators mandate that nurses lead field rescue teams

explanation: Spot on! Medical care doesn't wait until the patient reaches a hospital; it begins the moment they are pulled out, right at the boundary of the danger zone.

question: Which action shows the best emotional support for a patient dealing with infertility?

options.A: Telling the patient to stop worrying because everything happens for a reason
options.B: Listening actively and validating the patient's emotional grief
options.C: Avoiding the topic of children during all health conversations
options.D: Focusing solely on physical medication administration schedules

explanation: Well done! Infertility brings deep emotional pain. Listening without judgment helps patients process their grief in a safe space.

question: How do modified utensils with built-in grips help a patient with failing fine motor control?

options.A: They compensate for weak grip strength and hand tremors
options.B: They completely cure the underlying nerve degeneration
options.C: They prevent the patient from feeling hungry
options.D: They make the food taste better and digest faster

explanation: Specialized grips provide better purchase for weak hands, allowing the patient to continue feeding themselves without assistance. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h5)

question: What is the main benefit of using direct observation during a community survey?

options.A: It replaces the need to ever talk to local political leaders
options.B: It eliminates the need for any data analysis or calculations
options.C: It allows the nurse to see actual living and environmental conditions firsthand
options.D: It guarantees that no member of the community will fall sick

explanation: Observation lets nurses witness reality directly without relying on what people say or what old records report. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h5)

question: Which government tier is primarily responsible for managing Primary Health Care centers?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Health
options.B: Private pharmaceutical boards
options.C: International donor agencies
options.D: Local Government Area

explanation: Primary health care services in Nigeria are closest to the grassroots and are managed by the local government authorities. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h2)

question: Oxygen needs to move quickly across the tiny air sacs in the lungs. Which type of tissue lines these healthy air sacs?

options.A: Simple squamous epithelium
options.B: Transitional epithelium
options.C: Simple columnar epithelium
options.D: Stratified squamous epithelium

explanation: Simple squamous cells are super thin and flat, making them the perfect 'shortcut' for gases like oxygen to slip across.

question: Which of these is NOT a job of the hospital infection control unit regarding public health?

options.A: Notifying health authorities about dangerous reportable diseases
options.B: Collaborating on community-wide disease tracking efforts
options.C: Writing new tax laws for local healthcare businesses
options.D: Sharing local infection trend data with government agencies

explanation: Spot on! Tax laws are handled by government financial bodies, not hospital infection units.

question: What are the three core elements that make up Evidence-Based Practice (EBP)?

options.A: Financial cost, administrative goals, and staff availability
options.B: Hospital policy, doctor orders, and nursing intuition
options.C: Research evidence, clinical expertise, and patient values
options.D: Textbook theory, peer pressure, and trial-and-error

explanation: Brilliant! EBP is a sweet spot that combines what science proves, what your clinical skills tell you, and what the patient actually prefers.

question: Why does leftover tissue inside the uterus sharply increase the risk of infection?

options.A: It lowers the body temperature below normal levels.
options.B: It stops the liver from producing infection-fighting proteins.
options.C: It provides an ideal environment for bacteria to multiply.
options.D: It directly inactivates all circulating white blood cells.

explanation: Bacteria love stagnant, dead tissue mixed with blood! Leftover tissue creates a cozy breeding ground where bacteria can easily multiply and cause infection.

question: Which communication trick helps a nurse truly understand what a patient normally eats?

options.A: Assuming all patients eat the same traditional hospital diet
options.B: Handing out a pamphlet and asking if they can read
options.C: Reading a strict list of forbidden foods and waiting for agreement
options.D: Asking open-ended questions about what foods the patient eats at home

explanation: Open-ended questions like 'Tell me what you usually eat in a day' invite honest chats and help you give advice that fits their real life.

question: What is a strict safety rule for a patient being discharged after receiving sedation for an endoscopy?

options.A: They must have a responsible adult escort to take them home.
options.B: They must sign a new consent form before leaving the clinic.
options.C: They must stay in the hospital ward for at least three days.
options.D: They must avoid eating solid food for an entire week.

explanation: Because sedatives stay in the system for hours, patients are not allowed to go home alone or drive themselves. They need a trusted companion!

question: A nurse wants to address high salt intake in a local market. What should be the very first step?

options.A: Engage market vendors in a discussion about how they view salt use in local foods
options.B: Ban the sale of heavily salted processed snacks within the market stalls
options.C: Organize a mandatory lecture hall seminar for all registered market traders
options.D: Distribute brightly coloured pamphlets detailing the dangers of hypertension

explanation: Brilliant! True nursing care starts with listening. Always involve the community and understand their perspective before trying to change their habits.

question: Why is teaching a mother the correct way for her baby to latch crucial during breastfeeding?

options.A: It guarantees the infant will sleep through the night
options.B: It stops the baby from spitting up any milk
options.C: It prevents maternal nipple pain and ensures effective milk transfer
options.D: It forces the mother's milk to change from colostrum instantly

explanation: A good latch is a win-win: it keeps the mother's nipples safe from painful cracks and helps the baby get a full tummy efficiently! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h4)

question: What is the most effective way to improve community participation in rural immunization drives?

options.A: Relying solely on written posters placed inside clinic walls
options.B: Stopping all routine clinic visits to focus only on mass rallies
options.C: Engaging local community and religious leaders as advocates
options.D: Punishing parents who fail to bring their babies on time

explanation: Working with respected community and religious leaders helps build local trust and encourages families to accept and support immunization programs. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h8)

question: At what level does management happen in a hospital?

options.A: Only at the executive board room level
options.B: Exclusively within the hospital pharmacy department
options.C: At every level from charge nurse to director
options.D: Strictly during annual government audits

explanation: Management isn't just for bosses in suits! From frontline charge nurses managing the ward to senior directors, everyone plays a leadership role.

question: What is a key way a nurse advocates for a patient with poorly controlled pain?

options.A: Checking vital signs and ignoring what the patient says
options.B: Telling the patient to endure the pain so they don't get used to drugs
options.C: Waiting until the patient begs for stronger medicine
options.D: Working with the doctor to update an ineffective pain plan

explanation: As a nurse, you are the patient's voice. If their current medication isn't working, speak up and collaborate with the medical team to find a better solution!

question: How does a harsh blame culture negatively affect quality assurance efforts?

options.A: It causes patients to leave the hospital against medical advice
options.B: It drives staff to hide mistakes rather than report them for team learning
options.C: It speeds up the process of patient discharge too much
options.D: It forces the hospital to buy more expensive medical drugs

explanation: When people are afraid of harsh punishments, mistakes get swept under the rug. An open, supportive culture helps us learn and grow instead!

question: What is the main sign of complicated grief?

options.A: A normal, healthy reaction that resolves completely within two weeks
options.B: Physical illness caused strictly by lack of proper vitamin nutrition
options.C: Intense grief symptoms that remain severe and debilitating long after the loss
options.D: Complete absence of any emotional sadness following the death of a spouse

explanation: You got it! Complicated grief happens when a person gets stuck in deep, unyielding pain that stops them from getting back to daily life.

question: A nurse notices a sudden rise in wound infections on the surgical ward. What makes surveillance data valuable here?

options.A: It proves that surgery should be temporarily stopped
options.B: It helps identify a pattern to stop further infections
options.C: It allows the nurse to blame the cleaning staff
options.D: It ensures the patients get discharged faster

explanation: Tracking infection patterns gives clues about the source so corrective action can happen fast. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h2)

question: What is the main goal of quality improvement in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Continuous and structured refinement of care systems
options.B: Increasing the cost of specialized medical treatments
options.C: Reducing the overall number of employed nurses
options.D: Punishing staff members who make medication errors

explanation: You've got this! Quality improvement is all about making systems and care processes better over time, rather than pointing fingers or blaming individuals when mistakes happen.

question: What is the very first thing a nurse educator should do when planning a training program for staff?

options.A: Booking a large hotel conference hall
options.B: Printing out attendance certificates
options.C: Conducting a needs assessment
options.D: Purchasing expensive audiovisual equipment

explanation: Before teaching, you have to ask: what do the nurses actually need to learn? A needs assessment helps find the gaps so the training is super useful.

question: What is the correct nursing action when a mentally competent adult client refuses a prescribed blood transfusion?

options.A: Respect the refusal, educate the client on the risks, and notify the attending doctor
options.B: Threaten to discharge the client immediately from the hospital ward
options.C: Call security officers to hold the client down during the procedure
options.D: Administer the blood transfusion secretly while the client is sleeping

explanation: Competent adults have the right to refuse treatment, and nurses must document this while informing the medical team. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h4)

question: Which qualitative approach specifically focuses on exploring the lived experience of a concept?

options.A: Ethnography
options.B: Phenomenology
options.C: Clinical trial
options.D: Grounded theory

explanation: You can remember this easily: Phenomenology looks at 'phenomena' or lived experiences to uncover what a specific human experience truly feels like.

question: What is the most common opportunistic infection and leading cause of death in people with HIV?

options.A: Tetanus
options.B: Tuberculosis
options.C: Cholera
options.D: Malaria

explanation: Tuberculosis (TB) is the top opportunistic infection we watch out for in patients with weakened immune systems. Catching it early saves lives!

question: Why do Nigerian healthcare facilities need a clear waste management plan and ongoing staff training?

options.A: To reduce the number of patients visiting outpatient departments
options.B: To bridge the gap between written safety policies and actual clinical practice
options.C: To eliminate the need for electricity in hospital laboratories
options.D: To qualify for international sports tournament sponsorships

explanation: Having a rulebook on paper isn't enough—training ensures everyone actually follows safe habits on the ward every single day!

question: A clinic nurse manager receives a fresh supply of donor-funded malaria test kits. What is her immediate duty regarding these items?

options.A: Ensure proper inventory tracking, prevent wastage, and report usage accurately
options.B: Distribute all kits to administrative staff members instead of sick patients
options.C: Sell the test kits to private pharmacies to generate personal allowances
options.D: Hide the kits in a storeroom until the international donors leave the country

explanation: As a nurse managing donor supplies, keeping careful records, preventing waste, and reporting accurately is vital to keep the program accountable.

question: A clinic buys an expensive new lab machine instead of hiring two community health nurses. What is the opportunity cost here?

options.A: The financial cost of maintaining the new laboratory machine
options.B: The total budget allocated to the hospital for the entire year
options.C: The electricity used to power the laboratory equipment daily
options.D: The services and community health work provided by the two nurses

explanation: Exactly. By picking the machine, the clinic gave up the care those two nurses would have delivered to the community. That's the price of the choice! [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h2)

question: What was the main goal of classical management theory in the workplace?

options.A: Emotional counseling for all employees
options.B: Efficiency and standardized tasks
options.C: Flexible work hours and remote shifts
options.D: Democratic voting on all organizational policies

explanation: Classical management was all about maximum speed, clear chains of command, and doing tasks the exact same way every time like a machine.

question: Why is keeping a client's HIV test results completely confidential so crucial?

options.A: It removes the need for follow-up clinical appointments
options.B: It protects clients from social stigma and discrimination
options.C: It stops healthcare workers from keeping medical records
options.D: It ensures the laboratory processes blood samples faster

explanation: You got it! Because HIV still carries heavy social stigma, keeping results private shields patients from unfair treatment by family or community.

question: Which level of government in Nigeria typically manages primary health centers?

options.A: Private pharmaceutical firms
options.B: Federal ministries exclusively
options.C: Local government councils
options.D: International donors

explanation: Primary healthcare delivery is primarily the responsibility of local government authorities in the Nigerian health system. [learn more](GST321_U6_T3#GST321_U6_T3_h3)

question: What does the presence of thick meconium-stained amniotic fluid usually indicate?

options.A: Rapid dilation of the maternal cervix
options.B: A normal and healthy progression of labour
options.C: Normal kidney function in a full-term baby
options.D: Previous foetal stress and bowel relaxation

explanation: Hypoxia relaxes the foetal anal sphincter, causing the baby to pass meconium into the amniotic fluid before delivery. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h3)

question: In community health nursing, who is considered your primary client?

options.A: The individual patient in a hospital bed
options.B: The entire community or population
options.C: The medical doctor in charge of the ward
options.D: The administrative management of the hospital

explanation: You've got this! While hospital nursing focuses on one patient at a time, community health nursing looks at the big picture and cares for the whole population.

question: What is a core public health strategy used to manage HIV here in Nigeria?

options.A: Quarantining all infected individuals in remote camps
options.B: Banning the import of foreign foods

question: How can Nigerian nurses break through barriers that keep them out of health planning rooms?

options.B: By working entirely in private clinics without government oversight

question: A patient with a history of a traumatic past birth is most likely to experience what during her current labour?

options.A: An automatic decrease in the duration of the first stage

options.C: Heightened anxiety and risk of emotional distress
options.D: Total immunity to contraction pain

question: What is the correct speed (rate) for giving breaths during neonatal positive pressure ventilation (PPV)?

options.A: 20 to 30 breaths per minute
options.B: 40 to 60 breaths per minute
options.C: 10 to 15 breaths per minute
options.D: 80 to 100 breaths per minute

question: Which specific protein found in grains triggers the immune reaction that damages the small intestine in celiac disease?

options.D: Casein

question: What is the main job of pepsinogen, which is released by the chief cells?

options.C: It breaks down proteins after being converted to active pepsin
options.D: It lubricates food particles so they slide easily down the esophagus

explanation: Chief cells release pepsinogen in a safe, inactive form. Once stomach acid turns it into pepsin, it gets straight to work digesting proteins from your food.

question: Why are confidentiality and safe spaces so vital when caring for survivors of violence in a hospital?

options.A: To encourage survivors to share their experiences without fear of stigma or retaliation
options.B: To hide the crime from law enforcement agencies
options.C: To ensure the hospital avoids paying taxes on patient care
options.D: To speed up the discharge process for the patient

question: Why have state governments in Nigeria introduced State Health Insurance Agencies alongside the federal scheme?

options.A: To stop international donors from funding local health programs
options.B: To reach informal sector workers and rural residents more effectively
options.C: To completely replace all federal public hospitals with private clinics

explanation: State schemes help capture local traders, artisans, and rural dwellers who are often missed by federal formal-sector plans. Great thinking!

question: What is the main reason for using the 'teach-back' method at the end of a counselling session?

options.A: Confirming that the patient truly understands the instructions
options.B: Filling remaining time on hospital shifts
options.C: Proving the nurse followed hospital protocol
options.D: Testing if the patient can read a medical dictionary

explanation: Having patients repeat instructions in their own words is a wonderful way to catch and clear up any misunderstandings before they go home.

question: Why must nurse managers actively supervise instead of just writing policies on paper?

options.A: Written policies alone cannot guarantee staff will follow them safely
options.B: Nurse managers have no other administrative duties assigned to them
options.C: Staff nurses prefer having constant supervision during every shift
options.D: Hospital accreditation bodies legally require daily verbal check-ins

explanation: Having a policy on paper is a good start, but checking actual practice ensures everyone is safe and rules are followed in real clinical situations.

question: What is a key clinical marker used to evaluate the success of long-term diabetes management?

options.A: Hemoglobin A1c trends
options.B: Shoe size measurements
options.C: Frequency of dental visits
options.D: Hair color and texture

explanation: That's it! Tracking A1c over time gives a clear, reliable picture of how steady blood sugar levels have been.

question: Which of these is a key feature of teacher-centred teaching methods?

options.A: The classroom has no formal structure or predefined schedule
options.B: The teacher observes quietly while students teach each other
options.C: The students spend all class time performing independent research
options.D: The educator acts as the primary information giver while learners listen

explanation: In a teacher-centred setup (like a classic lecture), the instructor does most of the talking and passes information directly to the listening students.

question: What is a key nursing duty during the disaster preparedness phase?

options.A: Conducting community education and hazard awareness training
options.B: Demolishing unsafe buildings before an earthquake occurs
options.C: Writing national disaster budget legislation
options.D: Importing foreign medical equipment without authorization

explanation: Well done! Getting ready means educating the public so everyone knows what to do before an emergency strikes.

question: As a nurse, why should you understand lab values instead of just looking at the high or low flags?

options.A: Because laboratory printers frequently misprint the normal reference ranges
options.B: Because nurses are legally required to diagnose medical diseases
options.C: Because numbers help the nurse anticipate complications and plan safer care
options.D: Because doctors do not look at blood reports until discharge

explanation: You're not just memorizing numbers for an exam! Connecting lab values to real body signs helps you spot trouble early and keep your patient safe.

question: What emotional need is especially important for elderly family members?

options.A: Trying to fit in with teenage trends
options.B: Feeling respected and protected from loneliness
options.C: Wanting zero help from anyone at all
options.D: Living in high-stress, competitive environments

explanation: As people age and face physical changes, knowing they are valued, respected, and not forgotten keeps their spirits high and emotional health intact.

question: How does trial leave differ mainly from occasional leave?

options.A: Trial leave is only given to patients who refuse oral medications
options.B: Trial leave lasts much longer, often weeks or months, acting as a test for discharge
options.C: Trial leave requires the patient to stay inside a locked community center
options.D: Trial leave completely severs the patient's connection to the hospital

explanation: Trial leave is an extended test run lasting weeks or months to see if the patient is truly ready to head home permanently.

question: What happens when a research checklist turns your observations into simple checkmarks?

options.A: It turns descriptive notes into countable data for statistics
options.B: It automatically publishes the findings in a journal
options.C: It removes all potential errors from the research process
options.D: It changes qualitative research into a medical prescription

explanation: Tick marks make counting things super easy, which lets you run simple math and stats on your findings later.

question: Why does a malnourished patient usually take longer to recover from an infection?

options.A: Malnourished patients always refuse their oral medications
options.B: Hospital insurance policies automatically extend stays for underweight individuals
options.C: Their body lacks the nutritional fuel needed to fight infection and heal
options.D: Doctors cannot discharge anyone who has lost any body weight

explanation: You've got this! Healing requires energy and raw materials. Without them, recovery slows down and complications take longer to clear up.

question: What type of tissue makes up uterine fibroids?

options.A: Malignant epithelial tissue
options.B: Infected lymphatic fluid
options.C: Hardened calcified bone
options.D: Benign smooth muscle cells

explanation: Correct! Fibroids (also called leiomyomas) are simply non-cancerous growths made of the uterus's own smooth muscle cells. Nothing to panic about!

question: What structural adaptation do many veins have to prevent the backward flow of blood?

options.A: Fenestrated pore membranes
options.B: Continuous smooth muscle rings
options.C: Thick elastic outer layers
options.D: Internal one-way valves

question: A newly admitted resident is very quiet and refuses to interact with others. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Immediately discharge the resident back home for family care
options.B: Prescribe a mild sedative medication to calm their anxiety
options.C: Ignore the behavior since adjustment to a new home takes weeks
options.D: Conduct a comprehensive holistic assessment including psychological and social history

explanation: Spot on! Before jumping to conclusions, a warm, thorough assessment helps us find out if they are dealing with depression or fear so we can support them properly.

question: Why should a nurse teach a patient with diabetic foot neuropathy to test bathwater with their elbow instead of their feet?

options.A: Numbness in the feet prevents the patient from accurately sensing water temperature, risking scald burns
options.B: Elbow skin contains specialized sweat glands that neutralize toxic minerals found in tap water
options.C: Hot water causes immediate and permanent paralysis of the small motor nerves in the toes
options.D: The skin on the feet is biologically incapable of absorbing heat evenly compared to the upper body

explanation: Because neuropathy takes away normal feeling in the feet, patients might step into water that's way too hot without realizing it until they get burned. Using the elbow helps keep them safe!

question: Why do doctors often combine surgery with radiation or chemotherapy?

options.A: To prevent the patient from losing too much weight
options.B: To make the patient immune to future infections
options.C: To permanently boost the patient's red blood cell count
options.D: To eliminate any remaining microscopic cancer cells left behind

explanation: Think of it as teamwork! Surgery removes the main tumor, but combination therapies help sweep up any tiny stray cancer cells that are too small to see. You are doing brilliantly!

question: Which of these is NOT a normal symptom of the postpartum blues?

options.A: Temporary fatigue from broken sleep patterns
options.B: Mild mood swings and unexpected crying spells
options.C: Severe delusions and thoughts of harming the infant
options.D: Feeling slightly overwhelmed by new responsibilities

explanation: Crying spells and feeling overwhelmed are totally normal as hormones shift. However, delusions or thoughts of hurting the baby are never normal blues—they are signs of a severe emergency like postpartum psychosis. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h6)

question: How do healthy lifestyle habits primarily help men dealing with mild andropause symptoms?

options.A: By stopping the liver from producing binding proteins
options.B: By improving body composition, energy levels, and mood
options.C: By entirely replacing the need for medical check-ups
options.D: By permanently reversing the decline of testicular hormone production

explanation: While lifestyle changes won't stop natural aging or hormone drops, eating well and exercising work wonders for boosting energy and keeping spirits high!

question: What is the main goal of the Basel Convention?

options.A: To control the movement and safe disposal of hazardous wastes across borders
options.B: To regulate the global trade of pharmaceutical medications
options.C: To set limits on greenhouse gas emissions from factories
options.D: To manage the disposal of standard household garbage in landfills

explanation: You've got this! The Basel Convention was set up specifically to stop the harmful practice of shipping dangerous industrial waste across international borders where it could harm communities.

question: What does the FIFO stock rotation rule stand for?

options.A: Free-Issue, Fixed-Order
options.B: Final-Inspection, First-Order
options.C: First-In, First-Out
options.D: Fast-Item, Fast-Out

question: Why is solid political backing so important for keeping fake drugs out of Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: It removes the need for trained pharmacists in community clinics
options.B: It allows politicians to personally manufacture essential vaccines
options.C: It guarantees that all drugs are imported free of import duties
options.D: It enforces regulatory oversight to prevent counterfeit drugs from entering the market

explanation: Correct! Agencies like NAFDAC need strong legal backing and political support to crack down on counterfeit medications and keep patients safe.

question: A patient with an undetectable viral load for over a year asks if they can still pass the virus sexually. What is the best response?

options.A: Transmission can only happen if they stop eating fresh fruits
options.B: They can only transmit the virus during the rainy season
options.C: Transmission is still just as likely as before starting treatment
options.D: The risk of sexual transmission is effectively zero as long as adherence is maintained

question: As a psychiatric nurse, how should you view a patient's mental health symptoms when you first meet them?

options.A: As deliberate choices made to upset family members
options.B: As proof that the patient lacks all willpower
options.C: As an attempt by the psyche to protect itself
options.D: As permanent brain damage that cannot heal

explanation: Every symptom has a backstory. When we view symptoms as the mind's clumsy way of shielding itself from pain, it becomes much easier to care for our patients without judgment.

question: Which of these is an example of non-pharmacological (drug-free) pain relief?

options.A: Applying a warm compress to a sore muscle
options.B: Administering a prescribed dose of oral ibuprofen
options.C: Dispensing a scheduled narcotic pain pill
options.D: Injecting intravenous morphine into the patient port

question: Which type of law is made through acts passed by government and legislative bodies?

options.A: Common law

question: What does MBO stand for in healthcare management?

options.A: Mandatory Bed Operations

question: Why must a nurse carefully inspect the skin over a joint before an intraarticular injection?

options.A: To determine the best clothing size for the patient

options.C: To check if the patient has any permanent tattoos on the limb

question: What is the bright triangular light reflex seen on a normal tympanic membrane called?

question: Who was a key pioneer of the Moral Treatment movement in France?

options.A: Sigmund Freud

question: Which waste products are eliminated from the body through sweat?

question: A patient is having a rising panic attack at home. What is the best immediate nursing action?

question: Why must you respect the 'wet contact time' when using a disinfectant?

options.A: Wet surfaces look cleaner to patients and visiting family members

options.C: Keeping the surface wet prevents dust from settling on medical equipment
options.D: The chemical needs adequate time to interact with and destroy microbial structures

question: What makes providing home health care different from working in a hospital ward?

options.D: The nurse operates inside the patient's private residence

question: Which stage of insect development is completely skipped when an insect goes through incomplete metamorphosis?

options.A: The egg stage

options.D: The larval stage

question: What is the primary purpose of an Electronic Health Record (EHR)?

options.D: To provide patients with a private diary of their daily symptoms

question: How should an emotionally intelligent leader respond to a nurse dealing with burnout?

question: What is a major duty of a medical social worker in a rehab setting?

question: What do we call the unwritten rules and expected behaviors in a community?

question: What is the primary purpose of conducting regular quality assurance audits in a day care facility?

options.C: To increase daily attendance fees for participating families

question: A client expresses fear that a contraceptive injection will cause permanent infertility based on rumors heard in the market. How should the nurse respond?

question: What is the big plus of choosing a no-scalpel vasectomy over the older method?

question: What is the main physiological purpose of the large intestine?

question: What is the main goal of a medical evacuation (medevac)?

options.A: To move a patient to a facility with higher-level care
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of hospital treatment
options.C: To clear crowded hospital beds for new admissions
options.D: To provide permanent long-term rehabilitation therapy

explanation: Medevac is all about bridging the gap! It safely transports patients from places with limited resources to specialized centers where they can get the exact treatment they need.

question: Why might a patient scheduled for bariatric (weight loss) surgery be put on a low-calorie diet beforehand?

options.A: Building up large leg muscle stores
options.B: Shrinking liver size to ease surgery
options.C: Preventing all post-operative pain

question: Why do we often view rural villagers and urban slum residents as vulnerable populations?

options.A: They possess unlimited financial resources for private clinics
options.B: They always reject traditional and modern medical treatments equally
options.C: They have complete immunity against all infectious diseases
options.D: They face severe barriers to accessing affordable and quality healthcare services

question: What is the main health benefit of early breast milk (colostrum) for a newborn?

question: What is the best immediate nursing action for an unconscious patient who is breathing on their own?

options.A: Force fluids by mouth to prevent dehydration during sleep

options.C: Prop them upright in bed to encourage deep lung breathing

question: What is one of the best ways patients can prevent malaria at home?

options.A: Avoiding all contact with domestic farm animals
options.B: Boiling all household cooking oil before use

question: What causes the nutritional paradox where a person is both overweight and undernourished?

question: When is it strictly necessary for a nurse to use soap and water instead of an alcohol hand rub?

question: Which statistical test should you use to compare test scores across three different nursing shifts?

question: How does a hospital's poor response to a nursing mistake affect the rest of the team?

options.C: It drives staff to leave the profession out of fear and burnout

question: Which structure is known as the natural pacemaker of the heart?

options.D: Atrioventricular node

question: Why is a urinary catheter put in place during emergency care for severe abortion complications?

options.A: To flush the bladder with antiseptics to kill germs
options.B: To keep the patient from moving around the ward
options.C: To monitor hourly urine output and check kidney function

question: Why are women in active labour usually advised not to eat heavy solid foods?

options.C: To stop the stomach from producing excessive digestive acid

question: Why is communication in IEC a two-way process rather than a one-way lecture?

question: What happens when a drug is tightly attached to blood proteins?

question: Why are community health programs that teach about local crops so effective at preventing disease?

options.B: They empower communities to use accessible foods to stay healthy
options.C: They rely entirely on expensive imported medications
options.D: They eliminate the need for any clinical healthcare workers

explanation: Exactly! Teaching people how to make the best of what's already growing around them builds long-lasting, self-reliant health habits.

question: Why do milk-borne disease outbreaks often hit many people in a neighborhood all at once?

options.A: Many consumers drank from the same contaminated batch of milk

options.C: Public water systems carry the bacteria through house pipes
options.D: Local weather changes activate dormant spores in the air

question: Why can't nurses just use one standard diet plan for every single patient?

options.A: Because physical, metabolic, and lifestyle needs vary greatly among people

options.C: Because food guides require a different plan for every day of the year

question: What do we call the brand-new cell formed right after an egg and sperm join together?

question: What is the main downside of using benzodiazepines for a long-term fix for anxiety?

question: What is the main goal of primary prevention strategies regarding gender-based violence?
