options.C: Treating physical injuries in the emergency room after an attack
options.D: Providing long-term counseling years after an assault

explanation: Primary prevention focuses on stopping the root causes of violence before any abusive incident takes place. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T12#GNS312_U4_T12_h4)

question: Why is a simulation laboratory considered a safe learning space for nursing students?

options.A: Instructors are not allowed to point out mistakes
options.B: Students are never evaluated on their performance
options.C: There is no pressure or stress during the exercises
options.D: Errors made during scenarios do not harm real patients

explanation: Because mannequins or actors are used instead of real people, students can make and learn from mistakes safely. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T8#GNS212_U4_T8_h1)

question: What is an important rule for a nurse educator when bringing new technology into a lesson?

options.A: The technology must support the learning objective rather than act as a mere distraction
options.B: The digital tools must be replaced with brand-new equipment every single month
options.C: The students must build the computer software themselves before class begins
options.D: The educator should avoid speaking and let the computer teach the entire course

explanation: Tech is awesome, but it should always serve a clear purpose—helping you understand the nursing concept better, not just acting as a flashy distraction.

question: How do bones react when you do regular physical exercise and put mechanical stress on them?

options.A: They become fragile and brittle because osteoclasts destroy the matrix
options.B: They stop all cellular remodeling to conserve mineral reserves
options.C: They become thicker and stronger through increased osteoblast activity
options.D: They convert entirely from compact bone into spongy bone tissue

explanation: Use them and strengthen them! Exercise signals bone-building osteoblasts to lay down more material, making bones tough.

question: During the early (compensated) stage of shock, why do the skin and limbs often feel cool and pale?

options.A: Red blood cells lose their oxygen-carrying capacity in peripheral tissues
options.B: The ambient room temperature directly lowers the peripheral skin temperature
options.C: Blood is shunted away from non-vital areas to protect the heart and brain
options.D: Superficial blood vessels dilate to release excess heat from the body core

explanation: Think of the body as a smart manager: when resources are low, it redirects blood away from the skin and tummy to keep vital organs like the heart and brain happy. That's why the hands and feet get cool and pale first!

question: Why is plotting a child's measurements over time better than taking just a single measurement?

options.A: It is the only legal requirement for pediatric hospital admission
options.B: It reveals individual growth trends rather than just a one-time snapshot
options.C: It eliminates all possible errors made during the weighing process
options.D: It removes the need to use standard growth charts

explanation: Think of it like a movie versus a single photograph. One measurement only shows you right now, but tracking over time shows the real direction and speed of the child's development.

question: Why does emergency assessment focus on stabilizing the patient before investigating the cause?

options.A: Because nurses are not legally allowed to review past medical records
options.B: Because doctors prefer not to read detailed patient histories
options.C: Because laboratory tests are generally inaccurate in emergency rooms
options.D: Because stabilizing critical threats prevents patient deterioration and death

explanation: Saving a life always comes before finding out why the emergency happened. Keep the patient breathing and stable first!

question: What is polypharmacy generally defined as?

options.A: Stopping all medications abruptly without advice
options.B: Taking five or more medications concurrently
options.C: Injecting a single drug twice a day
options.D: Using only traditional herbs for chronic illnesses

explanation: Polypharmacy refers to the use of multiple drugs at the same time, commonly set at a threshold of five or more. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h3)

question: In a hospital, what do we mean by 'interdepartmental relationships'?

options.A: The personal friendships formed between nurses on the same shift
options.B: How different professional groups work together across hospital boundaries
options.C: The financial transactions between the hospital and medical suppliers
options.D: How doctors communicate exclusively with senior nursing staff

explanation: You've got this! Interdepartmental relationships simply mean teamwork and smooth communication between different units or departments in the hospital—like pharmacy working hand-in-hand with the ward.

question: What is the main goal of disease surveillance in community health?

options.A: To punish communities that fail to maintain basic sanitation
options.B: To eliminate all vector insects using chemical sprays
options.C: To detect and monitor disease patterns and potential reservoirs early
options.D: To manufacture and distribute expensive pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: Surveillance is like our radar system—it helps nurses spot disease trends and catch outbreaks before they blow up.

question: Why do community health nurses need to work alongside social workers and police when tackling streetism?

options.A: Multi-sectoral collaboration is needed because poverty, law, and health are all interconnected
options.B: Police officers are the only ones permitted to administer immunizations
options.C: Nurses are legally prohibited from speaking directly to children outdoors
options.D: Social workers handle all medical diagnoses while nurses write laws

explanation: Exactly! Streetism is a complex problem involving health, social welfare, and the law, so different professionals must team up to solve it.

question: What usually triggers a flexor or withdrawal reflex?

options.A: An increase in body temperature during physical exercise
options.B: A painful stimulus such as stepping on a sharp object
options.C: A sudden stretch caused by lifting a heavy object
options.D: A gentle tap on a tendon to test joint movement

explanation: Flexor reflexes are our automatic survival responses. When something hurts—like stepping on a pin—you pull away before you even have time to think about it.

question: What is the standard estimated life expectancy required for hospice admission?

options.A: Two years or less
options.B: One year or less
options.C: One month or less
options.D: Six months or less

explanation: Standard admission guidelines require a physician certification that the patient's life expectancy is six months or less. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T14#GNS324_U5_T14_h3)

question: What do we call the tiny, microscopic projections found right on the surface of intestinal lining cells?

options.A: Lacteals
options.B: Crypts
options.C: Plicae
options.D: Microvilli

explanation: Spot on! Microvilli sit right on top of the intestinal cells, forming a 'brush border' that gives an amazing boost to the surface area available for absorbing food.

question: What is usually the very first formal step when investigating a suspected disease outbreak?

options.A: Burn all personal belongings of infected residents
options.B: Verify the clinical diagnosis through laboratory testing
options.C: Construct a brand new tertiary care hospital
options.D: Close all international borders immediately

explanation: Before jumping to conclusions or panicking, public health teams must first confirm through lab tests that the suspected germ is actually there.

question: Why do nurses recommend using an ordinary cup instead of a feeding bottle for giving liquids to older infants?

options.A: Cups are much easier to clean and lower the risk of bacterial infections
options.B: Using bottles interferes with the natural development of the jawbone
options.C: Cups encourage the infant to drink larger volumes of liquid at one time
options.D: Infants cannot swallow liquids properly from a bottle after six months

explanation: Feeding bottles have tricky nooks and crannies that trap germs and are tough to sterilize. Cups are simple to wash and keep babies much safer from tummy bugs!

question: How is a community diagnosis similar to diagnosing an individual patient in the clinic?

options.A: Both focus exclusively on surgical intervention methods
options.B: Both identify problems to guide the choice of proper treatment or action
options.C: Both require the patient to stay overnight in a hospital bed
options.D: Both rely entirely on laboratory blood work results

explanation: Spot on. Whether it's one patient or a whole village, you have to figure out what is wrong first before you can choose the best way to help.

question: What happens to the baby's skull bones during moulding in labour?

options.A: They temporarily soften and melt
options.B: They separate and increase in width
options.C: They fracture to allow passage
options.D: They overlap to reduce head size

explanation: Great job! As the baby passes through the birth canal, the skull bones gently overlap at the sutures to make the head a bit smaller and help delivery go smoothly.

question: What pocket of pus can develop near the fallopian tube and ovary during a bad pelvic infection?

options.A: Cervical retention nodule
options.B: Endometrial polyp
options.C: Uterine fibroid cyst
options.D: Tubo-ovarian abscess

explanation: When upper reproductive infections get severe, pus can collect and form a painful pocket involving both the tube and the ovary, called a tubo-ovarian abscess.

question: What is the primary physiological defect in Type 1 diabetes mellitus?

options.A: Autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells
options.B: Peripheral resistance to the action of insulin
options.C: Temporary glucose intolerance during pregnancy
options.D: Excessive production of glucagon by the liver

explanation: Type 1 diabetes occurs when the immune system mistakenly attacks and destroys the insulin-producing beta cells in the pancreas. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h1)

question: Which tool is most essential for assessing the respiratory and cardiovascular systems?

options.A: Percussion hammer
options.B: Stethoscope
options.C: Otoscope
options.D: Tape measure

explanation: A stethoscope allows the nurse to hear internal sounds like heartbeats, valve closures, and air moving through lung fields. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h6)

question: What dangerous practice must nurses avoid to protect themselves from needlestick injuries?

options.A: Wearing clean gloves
options.B: Recapping used needles
options.C: Performing hand hygiene
options.D: Using safety-engineered devices

explanation: Recapping used needles is a primary cause of accidental needlestick injuries in clinical settings and must be avoided. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is the main reason for using a gait belt during a patient transfer?

options.A: To provide a secure handhold for the nurse to support the patient
options.B: To monitor the patient's breathing rate automatically
options.C: To lift the patient completely off the floor without help
options.D: To keep the patient's hospital gown tightly closed

explanation: A gait belt gives you a safe, firm grip around the patient's waist without having to awkwardly grab their clothes or arms.

question: Which of these is a key nursing task during a mass casualty incident?

options.A: Approving building permits for temporary relief shelters
options.B: Directing traffic flow on major highways leading out of the disaster zone
options.C: Assessing community vulnerability and managing casualty sorting areas
options.D: Distributing military weapons to community vigilante groups

explanation: Nurses are brilliant at triage (sorting patients by urgency) and figuring out community health risks during crises.

question: What is the main job of chemotherapy in cancer treatment?

options.A: To cool down inflamed skin tissues
options.B: To physically remove large solid tumors
options.C: To supply essential vitamins to the blood
options.D: To target and destroy rapidly dividing cells

explanation: You've got this! Chemotherapy drugs travel through the body specifically seeking out and killing cells that divide very quickly, which is what cancer cells love to do. Great job learning the basics!

question: What is a common barrier to tele-nursing in rural areas?

options.A: Strict government laws banning telephone conversations
options.B: Digital illiteracy and lack of modern devices
options.C: An excess of high-end personal computers in every home
options.D: Patients refusing care because they live too close to clinics

explanation: Spot on. Many rural dwellers might not own smartphones or know how to navigate digital apps easily.

question: What is the main goal of evaluating healthcare objectives?

options.A: To understand barriers and adapt strategies for better patient care.
options.B: To reduce the number of working hours for nurses.
options.C: To justify cutting the budget of underperforming units.
options.D: To find staff members to blame when targets are missed.

explanation: Evaluation isn't about blaming people; it's about figuring out what roadblocks got in the way so we can improve patient care next time.

question: Which statement best demonstrates empathy toward a client struggling with a new diagnosis?

options.A: You just need to follow your medication list every single day.
options.B: It must be really hard to adjust to these new lifestyle changes.
options.C: Why did you wait so long to see a doctor about your symptoms?
options.D: Everyone gets this disease eventually, so do not worry too much.

explanation: Acknowledging the client's emotional struggle shows empathy by validating their personal experience with the illness. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h4)

question: Why is it important for nurses to report both real vaccine reactions and random health events that happen after vaccination?

options.A: To prove that pharmaceutical manufacturing companies are always at fault for patient illness
options.B: To automatically trigger immediate free hospital admission for every sick child
options.C: To help health authorities investigate and determine the true root cause of the incident
options.D: To legally punish mothers who bring their children late for routine clinic appointments

explanation: Reporting helps public health experts look at the facts, figure out what really happened, and keep immunization safe for everyone.

question: What is a very common emotional challenge for people dealing with untreated hearing loss?

options.A: Improved cognitive processing
options.B: Heightened sense of euphoria
options.C: Increased physical strength
options.D: Social isolation and depression

explanation: When it's hard to hear conversations, people often start pulling away from social gatherings, which can lead to loneliness and depression.

question: Why are women and children often the most vulnerable during forced displacement?

options.A: They are legally barred from entering any healthcare facility.
options.B: They face higher risks of exploitation, violence, and malnutrition.
options.C: They always travel faster than other members of the community.
options.D: They possess complete immunity against all infectious diseases.

explanation: When normal social supports break down, women and children face greater dangers regarding safety, abuse, and getting enough proper food.

question: Sometimes, tissue injury during an infection isn't just caused by the germ itself. What else can cause damage?

options.A: The body's own defense mechanisms damage healthy cells while fighting the germ.
options.B: The invading microbes block all blood flow to the skin surface.
options.C: The patient experiences a sudden drop in daily nutritional intake.
options.D: The pathogen directly dissolves every organ in the human body.

explanation: It's like friendly fire! Sometimes our immune system fights so fiercely that healthy tissues get caught in the crossfire.

question: Which nursing intervention provides a simple, non-pharmacological method to relieve primary dysmenorrhea?

options.A: Administering intravenous broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.B: Placing the client in an absolute flat supine position
options.C: Encouraging immediate high-impact interval training
options.D: Applying local heat therapy to the lower abdomen

explanation: Heat relaxes uterine smooth muscle and helps reduce the ischemic pain associated with menstrual cramps. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T7#GNS311_U1_T7_h7)

question: How should removable dentures be kept when the patient is not wearing them?

options.A: Wrapped up tight in dry gauze inside a bedside drawer
options.B: In a labeled container filled with water or soaking solution
options.C: Dropped in boiling water overnight to kill all germs
options.D: Left out in the open air on top of the locker table

explanation: Keeping dentures wet in a safe container stops the plastic material from bending out of shape and keeps them ready for use.

question: You enter a medication order into the computer, and a warning pops up about a bad drug interaction. What should you do next?

options.A: Ignore the pop-up window because computers frequently make mistakes
options.B: Turn off the computer system to prevent further alerts from showing up
options.C: Administer the medication immediately since the computer cannot override a doctor
options.D: Investigate the warning, verify the client's profile, and consult the prescribing physician

explanation: Always treat these alerts as a helpful safety net! Pause, double-check the patient and the order, and talk to the doctor before giving the drug. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h3)

question: According to the Spaulding classification, what level of processing is required for surgical instruments?

options.A: Basic washing with soap
options.B: High-level disinfection
options.C: Sterilization
options.D: Low-level disinfection

explanation: Surgical instruments are classified as critical items because they enter sterile tissues, so they must be fully sterilized. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h3)

question: How is a middle-range theory different from a grand nursing theory?

options.A: It is completely unproven and used only by student researchers
options.B: It applies strictly to hospital administration rather than patient care
options.C: It avoids using any concepts related to human behavior
options.D: It focuses on specific, manageable clinical situations rather than broad, universal ideas

explanation: Exactly. While grand theories try to explain all of nursing, middle-range theories zoom in on specific, everyday clinical situations that are easier to study.

question: What is the surest way to confirm a diagnosis of vulval cancer?

options.A: Pelvic ultrasound
options.B: Complete blood count
options.C: Urinalysis and culture
options.D: Tissue biopsy

explanation: Correct! Taking a small tissue sample (biopsy) is the only definitive way to confirm if a growth is truly cancerous.

question: What is the main goal of maternal home healthcare visits in our communities?

options.A: To bridge the gap between hospital services and community living
options.B: To distribute free prescription drugs to every household
options.C: To replace the need for hospital delivery entirely
options.D: To enforce strict hospital rules inside family compounds

explanation: Home visits let you bring health education and monitoring right to the doorstep of mothers who find it hard to visit the clinic regularly. You're making healthcare accessible where they live!

question: How does a prospective study differ fundamentally from a retrospective study?

options.A: Prospective studies look forward at future events, while retrospective studies look backward at past records
options.B: Prospective studies involve no data collection, while retrospective studies involve heavy data collection
options.C: Prospective studies are always qualitative, while retrospective studies are always quantitative
options.D: Prospective studies use animal subjects, while retrospective studies only use human patients

explanation: The core difference lies in the temporal orientation, with prospective starting in the present and moving forward, and retrospective starting in the present and looking backward. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T15#GNS224_U1_T15_h1)

question: Which of these would stop you from using a tympanic thermometer safely?

options.A: A buildup of earwax blocking the ear canal
options.B: The patient just drank some water
options.C: A history of mild seasonal allergies
options.D: Mild dehydration without a fever

explanation: Excess wax blocks the path to the eardrum, meaning the sensor won't catch the right heat radiation.

question: A student nurse visiting an elderly client notices a slippery bathtub with no support rails. What is the best immediate safety action?

options.A: Recommend installing grab bars and using a non-slip bath mat
options.B: Advise the client to stop bathing completely during the week
options.C: Tell the family to remodel the entire house immediately
options.D: Suggest moving the client to a hospital right away

explanation: Great choice! Adding simple items like grab bars and non-slip mats fixes the danger right away without needing drastic changes like moving out.

question: How do out-of-pocket purchases by patients for basic ward supplies affect hospital records?

options.A: They distort standard cost calculations because items are bought outside the system
options.B: They guarantee that all indirect costs are fully covered by the government
options.C: They make hospital accounting completely automatic and error-free
options.D: They eliminate the need for patient classification systems

explanation: When patients run out to buy their own routine supplies, the hospital's official records miss the true picture of what delivering care actually costs.

question: Which secondary source uses math and statistics to combine the results of many different studies?

options.A: Primary clinical trial
options.B: Narrative textbook chapter
options.C: Meta-analysis
options.D: Case study

explanation: Awesome! A meta-analysis pools numbers from several studies together to give us a powerful big-picture answer.

question: What is the primary purpose of instilling medication drops into the eye, ear, or nose?

options.A: To deliver slow-release nutrition directly into the blood
options.B: To completely flush out all natural body fluids
options.C: To provide direct local treatment to the affected area
options.D: To replace the need for all oral pain medications

explanation: Drops are applied straight to body cavities so the medicine works right where it is needed most. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h1)

question: How does population diversity affect the sample size you need for a study?

options.A: Diversity has no impact on the required number of participants
options.B: A more diverse population requires a smaller sample size
options.C: Diverse populations can only be studied using convenience sampling
options.D: A more diverse population requires a larger sample size

explanation: You got it! If the group has many different backgrounds and experiences, you need a bigger sample to capture all those variations accurately.

question: Which sign is a classic clue of right-sided heart congestion?

options.A: Complete loss of vision in both eyes
options.B: Sudden wheezing and frothy pink sputum
options.C: Severe sharp chest pain radiating to the jaw
options.D: Peripheral edema and jugular venous distension

explanation: When the right side backs up, blood dams up in the body's veins. This leads to swollen ankles (edema) and bulging neck veins (jugular venous distension).

question: What are the main signs that tell you it's time to grab and use an AED?

options.A: Confusion and slow, deep respirations
options.B: Severe chest pain and high blood pressure
options.C: Unresponsiveness and no normal breathing
options.D: Dizziness, sweating, and a racing pulse

explanation: Spotting cardiac arrest is key: if someone won't wake up and isn't breathing normally, get that AED ready right away!

question: A pregnant patient at 32 weeks comes in with bright red bleeding, and placenta previa is suspected. What action must the nurse NEVER do?

options.A: Performing a digital vaginal examination
options.B: Applying an electronic fetal monitor
options.C: Starting a large-bore intravenous line
options.D: Checking maternal blood pressure

explanation: Never put your fingers inside when placenta previa is suspected! Doing a digital exam can poke the placenta and trigger massive, life-threatening bleeding. Always check the ultrasound first. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T6#GNS121_U6_T6_h8)

question: Why do we carry out a re-audit near the end of a quality improvement cycle?

options.A: To find new reasons to query junior nursing staff members
options.B: To see if the corrective actions successfully improved care
options.C: To comply with international travel laws for nurses
options.D: To increase the amount of paperwork stored in the archive

explanation: Spot on! A re-audit helps us check whether the changes we put in place actually solved the problems we found during our first check.

question: A nurse thinks safety rules only matter in big factories and ignores small offices in the building. Where is the mistake in this thinking?

options.A: Nursing councils have no say over non-manufacturing environments
options.B: Administrative offices are completely exempt from all laws
options.C: Workplace safety regulations extend to offices and small-scale enterprises as well
options.D: Only human resources are responsible for office building safety

explanation: Spot on! Safety laws apply everywhere people work—even in small offices, not just heavy industries.

question: Your patient has an overactive thyroid (high T3 and T4). What sign would you most expect to see?

options.A: High blood sugar and frequent urination
options.B: Severe weight gain and feeling cold
options.C: Rapid weight loss and feeling warm
options.D: Slow resting heart rate and constant sleepiness

explanation: High thyroid hormone levels put the body's engine on overdrive! Patients burn through calories super fast, so they tend to lose weight quickly and feel hot all the time.

question: How can community health nurses help traditional practitioners who perform FGM?

options.A: Help provide alternative means of livelihood so they stop cutting
options.B: Force them to leave the community without any financial help
options.C: Ignore their economic needs and threaten them with jail only
options.D: Hire them in the hospital clinic to perform minor surgeries

explanation: Great job! Many practitioners rely on FGM to make a living, so teaching new skills and providing other sources of income helps them stop permanently.

question: How do tight spaces on a boat affect how medical supplies are kept?

options.A: Supplies must be tightly organized and secured so they do not slide around.
options.B: Medical bays are built with expandable walls that stretch during emergencies.
options.C: Nurses are forced to store all extra equipment on the outside deck.
options.D: Only a single box of bandages is allowed on board at any time.

explanation: Spot on! Because ship clinic spaces are compact, loose items can fly around during rough weather, so everything has to be safely locked down.

question: Why do nurses routinely check a urine sample (urinalysis) when evaluating new urine leaks?

options.A: To check for a urinary tract infection
options.B: To determine the patient's blood type
options.C: To screen for prostate cancer markers
options.D: To measure exact kidney filtration rates

explanation: Infections can irritate the bladder and cause sudden leaks. Ruling out an infection is always a smart first step in nursing assessment.

question: What is the primary purpose of government food assistance programs?

options.A: To force citizens to purchase locally grown organic vegetables
options.B: To regulate the exact calorie intake of every household
options.C: To completely eliminate the need for private grocery stores
options.D: To help protect vulnerable populations from hunger and poor nutrition

explanation: Social safety nets exist to ensure that low-income families and individuals can access enough food to stay healthy. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T020#GNS227_U2_T020_h7)

question: Which ventilator mode gives a set volume when the patient tries to breathe, but also guarantees a minimum backup rate if they get too tired?

options.A: Control mode
options.B: Assist-Control mode
options.C: Continuous Positive Airway Pressure
options.D: Pressure Support mode

explanation: In Assist-Control mode, the machine is always watching: if the patient breathes, the machine helps out with a full breath. If the patient stops trying, the machine's timer steps in to breathe for them!

question: Why do vulvitis and vaginitis often happen together?

options.A: The vaginal canal produces secretions that protect the vulva from damage.
options.B: Both areas share the exact same hormonal receptors.
options.C: Infections always start inside the uterus first.
options.D: The physical closeness of the external and internal tissues allows irritation to spread easily.

explanation: Think of it like neighbors—because the vulva and vagina live right next to each other, an infection or irritation in one can easily reach the other. Great job thinking through clinical anatomy!

question: Which eye finding is a classic sign that death has occurred?

options.A: Constricted pupils in bright light
options.B: Rapid involuntary blinking
options.C: Severe swelling of the eyelids
options.D: Fixed and dilated pupils

explanation: Well done! When the brainstem stops working, the pupils stop reacting to light and stay wide and fixed.

question: Which of the following is classified as a shockable cardiac arrest rhythm?

options.A: Sinus bradycardia
options.B: Pulseless Electrical Activity
options.C: Ventricular Fibrillation
options.D: Asystole

explanation: Ventricular Fibrillation causes chaotic quivering that responds well to an emergency electrical shock. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T4#GNS315_U4_T4_h3)

question: What does a public health nurse focus on most during community outreach?

options.A: Performing emergency appendectomies in a village square
options.B: Educating mothers on childhood immunization and sanitation
options.C: Installing borehole water pumps for the village
options.D: Prescribing chemotherapy for advanced cancer patients

explanation: Exactly! Public health nurses are community champions. They focus heavily on disease prevention, health education, and keeping moms and babies smiling and healthy.

question: Which mental health issue is most commonly diagnosed in survivors of severe violence?

options.A: Bipolar mood disorder
options.B: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD)
options.C: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)
options.D: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD)

explanation: Correct! Survivors of intense physical, emotional, or sexual trauma very often develop PTSD because of the deep impact of their experience.

question: What is the specific, go-to antidote for a paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose?

options.A: Naloxone
options.B: Atropine
options.C: Flumazenil
options.D: Acetylcysteine

explanation: You'll see this often in the ward! Acetylcysteine saves the liver by restocking its natural protector (glutathione) just in time before paracetamol metabolites cause damage.

question: What makes an abortion officially classified as 'unsafe' by global health standards?

options.A: Any pregnancy loss occurring naturally during the first trimester
options.B: A procedure done by unskilled persons or in poor environments
options.C: A termination done without proper surgical instruments
options.D: A medical termination performed past the first trimester

explanation: An unsafe abortion happens when the procedure is carried out by people without proper training, in dirty or poorly equipped places, or both. Knowing this helps us understand why access to safe care is so vital!

question: Which of these is NOT something a community health nurse would focus on during an IDP camp assessment?

options.A: Environmental waste and refuse disposal sites
options.B: Private stock market investment portfolios
options.C: Availability and safety of drinking water
options.D: Presence of vulnerable pregnant women and infants

explanation: Nurses focus on health, safety, and sanitation needs—not financial investments!

question: Why is it important to read the ingredient list on packaged foods?

options.A: To determine the precise market price of the item
options.B: To check for hidden sugars, sodium, and potential allergens
options.C: To calculate the exact weight of the empty container
options.D: To find out which factory manufactured the product

explanation: Ingredient lists reveal what is actually inside the food, helping patients avoid allergens and manage conditions like hypertension or diabetes. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T006#GNS227_U3_T006_h5)

question: During which step of the nursing process do standardized care plans and pathways guide your choices the most?

options.A: Diagnosis
options.B: Evaluation
options.C: Assessment
options.D: Planning

explanation: You got it! The planning phase is where you map out the specific steps and pathways to help your patient reach their health goals.

question: What do the blood vessels in your skin do when your body temperature gets too high and you need to cool down?

options.A: They thicken permanently
options.B: They vasodilate
options.C: They collapse entirely
options.D: They vasoconstrict

explanation: You're right! They vasodilate (open wider) to bring more warm blood close to the surface, letting excess body heat escape into the air.

question: Why is simple bed making considered an essential clinical nursing skill rather than just housekeeping?

options.A: It is the only duty a nursing student can do alone
options.B: It replaces the need for daily patient bathing
options.C: It directly promotes patient comfort, safety, and skin integrity
options.D: It lowers the overall room temperature for fever management

explanation: Spot on! A clean, well-made bed is the foundation of a safe healing environment. It protects vulnerable skin and keeps your patients comfortable.

question: A nurse notices a resident's food intake has dropped sharply over two weeks. What is the best next step?

options.A: Collaborate with the interprofessional team to update the care plan
options.B: Wait for the annual assessment to record the weight loss
options.C: Discharge the resident to an assisted living facility
options.D: Stop monitoring meal intake since preferences change

explanation: Exactly right! Care plans are living documents. When a change happens, we team up with dietitians and doctors right away to update the plan and help the resident.

question: What is a key benefit of presenting research at a scientific conference?

options.A: Guaranteeing automatic acceptance into international print magazines
options.B: Eliminating the need to ever write a formal research paper
options.C: Getting immediate feedback and networking with other professionals
options.D: Receiving a cash prize from the hospital management board

explanation: Conferences allow researchers to talk directly with peers, answer questions on the spot, and build useful professional relationships. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h3)

question: A patient moves to another city and visits a new hospital network. Which system is designed to seamlessly transfer their complete medical history to the new care team?

options.A: Paper nursing kardex
options.B: Electronic Medical Record
options.C: Electronic Health Record
options.D: Local pharmacy ledger

explanation: EHRs are built specifically for interoperability, allowing patient data to follow them across different healthcare networks and providers. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is the chemical neurotransmitter released at the neuromuscular junction?

options.A: Serotonin
options.B: Acetylcholine
options.C: Dopamine
options.D: Norepinephrine

explanation: Acetylcholine is released from motor neurons to cross the synapse and stimulate muscle fiber membranes. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h3)

question: When assessing muscle strength, how should the nurse evaluate the limbs?

options.A: By measuring the exact circumference with a tape
options.B: Bilaterally to compare both sides of the body
options.C: Only after administering pain medication
options.D: Only on the dominant side to save time

explanation: Comparing opposite sides helps identify localized weakness or asymmetry caused by neurological injury. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is the most common and trusted way to sterilize metal surgical tools?

options.A: Boiling in water for twenty minutes
options.B: Steam under pressure in an autoclave
options.C: Ultraviolet radiation in a glass cabinet
options.D: Immersion in liquid bleach solution

explanation: The autoclave is the workhorse of the CSSD! Using high-pressure steam is fast, affordable, and extremely reliable for metal instruments.

question: What is a major problem for hospitals when national economic funding is low?

options.A: Surplus funding for specialized nursing research
options.B: Excessive availability of advanced medical technology
options.C: Immediate reduction in patient admission rates across all wards
options.D: Severe shortages of basic supplies and heavy workloads

explanation: You've probably seen this in practice: low funding means fewer gloves, less medication, and exhausted staff carrying heavy workloads. You are doing great learning about this!

question: What is the term for the process where the mother's body returns to its pre-pregnant state after delivery?

options.A: Duplication
options.B: Hypertrophy
options.C: Hemodilution
options.D: Involution

explanation: Involution refers to the rapid process by which the uterus and other body systems return to their non-pregnant size and condition. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h2)

question: A patient reacts badly to a medication, but their vitals are now stable. What is the next best step?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately to avoid further complications
options.B: Inform the patient and family honestly about what happened
options.C: Wait several weeks to see if the family asks any questions
options.D: Hide the medication chart so nobody discovers the mistake

explanation: Once the patient is stable, being open and honest with them and their family is the essential next step.

question: You receive your handoff report and hear about four different tasks. Which one needs your immediate action?

options.A: A non-urgent blood pressure check for a stable patient
options.B: A missing signature on a nursing admission form from yesterday
options.C: A patient reporting sudden chest pain and shortness of breath
options.D: A routine discharge education session scheduled for the afternoon

explanation: Spot on! Chest pain and trouble breathing point to an emergency that takes priority over any routine paperwork.

question: How does normal aging usually affect the body's homeostatic control systems?

options.A: They increase in functional reserve capacity across all organs
options.B: They stop using feedback loops and rely entirely on positive feedback
options.C: They become less efficient at responding to environmental stress
options.D: They speed up and become overly sensitive to minor changes

explanation: You've got it! As people grow older, their internal systems take a bit longer to bounce back from stress like extreme heat, cold, or sudden illness.

question: As a nurse, what is the quickest way to help a patient who is suddenly struggling to catch their breath due to lung cancer?

options.A: Laying the patient flat on their back in bed
options.B: Placing the patient in a high-Fowler's position
options.C: Encouraging rapid, shallow mouth breathing
options.D: Restricting all fluid intake for twelve hours

explanation: Spot on, nurse! Sitting the patient upright in a high-Fowler's position lets their chest expand fully, making it much easier to draw breath.

question: Which layer of the uterus gives it the strong power to push out a baby during labor?

options.A: Perimetrium
options.B: Epimetrium
options.C: Myometrium
options.D: Endometrium

explanation: Well done! The myometrium is made of thick, strong muscle that contracts powerfully during childbirth.

question: What is the big advantage of using the 'closed gloving' technique in theater?

options.A: It prevents bare hands from touching the outside of the sterile gloves
options.B: It eliminates the need to wear a surgical gown during the case
options.C: It keeps the sterile gloves warmer during long procedures
options.D: It allows the nurse to scrub hands much faster than usual

explanation: By keeping your hands tucked inside your gown sleeves, you can slide your gloves on without your bare skin ever touching the outside surface.

question: A nurse is caring for a patient who speaks a language the nurse does not understand, making medication education difficult. What is the best action to take?

options.A: Ask another patient in the ward to translate the medical terms
options.B: Skip the medication education entirely and just leave the pills on the bedside table
options.C: Request an official hospital interpreter to help explain the drug instructions
options.D: Refuse to give the prescribed drugs until the patient learns English

explanation: Using a trained professional interpreter ensures accurate communication and protects the patient's right to safe, informed care. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T3#GNS125_U3_T3_h7)

question: A nurse researcher wants local ward staff to immediately adopt a new fall-prevention protocol. Which dissemination channel is most effective?

options.A: Publishing a brief note on a personal entertainment blog
options.B: Holding a hands-on clinical workshop and ward training session
options.C: Mailing hard copies of the raw data tables to the health minister
options.D: Submitting a lengthy letter to an international history journal

explanation: Hands-on workshops give frontline staff direct training and practice with new clinical protocols. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a core duty expected of a nurse, no matter where they work?

options.A: Performing major neurosurgical operations independently
options.B: Administering prescribed medications safely
options.C: Advocating for the health and safety of patients
options.D: Monitoring vital signs and clinical progress

explanation: Surgeries like brain operations are strictly done by trained surgeons, not nurses, regardless of whether it's a primary clinic or a tertiary hospital!

question: What does a drug's half-life represent in pharmacokinetics?

options.A: The time it takes for the body to absorb half of an oral dose
options.B: The time it takes for blood concentration of the drug to decrease by 50 percent
options.C: The exact number of hours a drug remains active in the stomach
options.D: The time required for the liver to metabolize half of the active ingredient

explanation: Half-life measures how long it takes for the amount of drug in the blood to drop down to half of its previous level. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T4#GNS125_U5_T4_h6)

question: A patient is given naloxone to wake them up and reverse a dangerous morphine overdose. What kind of drug action is this?

options.A: Absorption
options.B: Potentiation
options.C: Antagonism
options.D: Synergism

explanation: Spot on! Naloxone acts as a true antagonist—it rushes to the rescue, kicks the morphine off the receptors, and blocks its effects to save the patient.

question: Which macronutrient provides the highest amount of energy per gram?

options.A: Carbohydrate
options.B: Protein
options.C: Fat
options.D: Water

explanation: Fats provide nine calories per gram, which is more than double the energy density found in carbohydrates or proteins. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T009#GNS227_U6_T009_h3)

question: Why is advocacy often necessary alongside health education in community practice?

options.A: Health education is illegal without formal permission from community elders
options.B: Government officials only listen to nurses and ignore the local population
options.C: Advocacy replaces the need to teach people about proper nutrition and hygiene
options.D: Education alone cannot fix environmental and structural problems like lack of clean water

explanation: Even if people know what is healthy, structural barriers like poor infrastructure require political advocacy and community mobilization to fix. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T26#GNS225_U2_T26_h6)

question: What kind of data do you mainly collect in qualitative research?

options.A: Words, text, and descriptions of human experiences
options.B: Statistical percentages of patient readmissions
options.C: Exact laboratory blood chemistry measurements
options.D: Precise numerical vital signs recorded hourly

explanation: While quantitative loves numbers, qualitative loves words! It looks at interview notes and stories to understand human experiences.

question: How does discussing risk assessment openly help the pregnant mother?

options.A: It empowers her to understand danger signs and join healthcare decisions
options.B: It frightens her enough to ensure she obeys every hospital rule
options.C: It stops her from asking questions during labor
options.D: It proves to her family that nurses know everything about birth

explanation: Open communication helps the mother recognize when something is wrong and trust the care plan. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h2)

question: Which symptom is a very common clue that points specifically to COVID-19 over other flu-like viruses?

options.A: Sudden loss of taste or smell
options.B: Yellow discoloration of the skin
options.C: Uncontrollable muscle twitching
options.D: Severe swelling of the salivary glands

explanation: Spot on! Losing your sense of taste or smell (anosmia and ageusia) is a classic hallmark sign of a SARS-CoV-2 infection. Easy to remember for your clinicals!

question: Why must honey be strictly avoided for infants under one year of age?

options.A: It contains high levels of artificial food coloring
options.B: It always causes immediate childhood obesity
options.C: It carries a severe risk of causing infant botulism
options.D: It replaces the need for essential milk feeds

explanation: Honey can contain spores of the bacterium Clostridium botulinum, which immature infant digestive tracts cannot fight off safely. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h4)

question: Which symptom means a patient with diarrhoea should stop home treatment and see a doctor right away?

options.A: Mild rumbling sounds in the abdomen
options.B: Blood appearing in the stool
options.C: Mild fatigue after a long day
options.D: A slight drop in appetite

explanation: Blood in the stool is a red flag! It usually points to a nasty bacterial infection or injury to the gut lining that needs professional medical help.

question: Which of these is a common myth about infection control in home settings?

options.A: That handwashing helps reduce bacterial spread
options.B: That family members can transmit respiratory viruses
options.C: That the home environment is naturally germ-free
options.D: That used needles require special puncture-proof containers

explanation: Don't be fooled—homes are not naturally sterile! Good cleaning and hygiene habits are still a must everywhere.

question: How does vitamin C help your body when you eat it along with beans?

options.A: It increases the absorption of plant-based iron
options.B: It prevents the protein in beans from causing gas
options.C: It turns the complex carbohydrates into simple sugars
options.D: It slows down digestion so you feel full longer

explanation: Brilliant! Vitamin C acts like a helpful helper, making it much easier for your gut to absorb the iron found in plant foods like beans.

question: What is a common tobacco trend among young people in Nigerian cities today?

options.A: A total shift toward chewing raw tobacco leaves exclusively
options.B: A complete halt in all forms of smoking
options.C: The rising popularity of manufactured cigarettes and shisha
options.D: The replacement of tobacco with herbal medicinal teas

explanation: Smart marketing has made manufactured cigarettes and waterpipes (shisha) very popular among urban youth. Keep up the good work!

question: How does a procedure called marsupialization stop a Bartholin cyst from coming back?

options.A: By surgically removing the entire gland and surrounding tissue
options.B: By sealing the gland shut so it stops producing any fluid
options.C: By stitching the edges of the cyst open to create a permanent little pouch
options.D: By packing the internal cavity tightly with sterile gauze

explanation: Marsupialization sounds fancy, but it just means sewing the walls of the cyst open so it turns into a tiny pouch. This stops fluid from getting trapped again!

question: What is the go-to medication for stopping and preventing seizures in severe preeclampsia?

options.A: Diazepam tablets
options.B: Magnesium sulfate
options.C: Calcium gluconate
options.D: Hydralazine injection

explanation: You're doing great! Magnesium sulfate is the gold standard for managing eclamptic seizures and keeping mothers safe. A true midwifery essential!

question: A Nigerian ward experiences frequent equipment mix-ups during emergencies. Which simple, low-cost fix would help the most?

options.A: Requiring nurses to memorize every device manual word-for-word
options.B: Color-coding emergency trolley drawers and standardizing equipment placement
options.C: Stopping all patient admissions until brand new imported machines arrive
options.D: Firing all junior nurses to reduce crowding around the storage area

explanation: Simple visual aids like color-coding and tidy, consistent layouts save precious seconds during emergencies without needing expensive high-tech gear!

question: How can nurses best help prevent FGM within local communities?

options.A: By educating families and working with local leaders to change attitudes
options.B: By reporting every pregnant woman to international human rights courts
options.C: By offering safe, clean clinical alternatives for young girls
options.D: By focusing only on treating women who already have complications

explanation: Prevention relies on grassroots education and community engagement to address the root cultural drivers of FGM. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h5)

question: What simple inventory rule helps nurses make sure older ward medications are used before they expire?

options.A: Random batch sampling
options.B: Daily physical head count
options.C: Maximum-Minimum stock level
options.D: First-In, First-Out rule

explanation: Brilliant! The First-In, First-Out (FIFO) rule simply means the drugs that arrived first are the ones used first, preventing waste on the shelf.

question: Which nursing action helps most with the social and emotional challenges of chronic epilepsy?

options.A: Focusing solely on medication dosages and ignoring emotional health
options.B: Isolating the patient from family to reduce external stress
options.C: Encouraging the patient to hide their diagnosis from employers
options.D: Providing counseling resources and addressing social stigma

explanation: Epilepsy carries a lot of societal stigma in many communities. Offering support, education, and counseling helps patients build confidence and live full lives. You've got this! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T12#GNS222_U4_T12_h8)

question: Which detail is most important to include in your notes when charting routine hair care?

options.A: The exact minute the hair drying process started
options.B: Condition of the scalp and any abnormal findings
options.C: The total cost of the hair care products used
options.D: The exact brand of shampoo preferred by the nurse

explanation: Always focus your documentation on clear clinical facts, such as how the scalp looks and any unusual signs you spot. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h6)

question: What health issue do we frequently see in children with heavy gut parasite infections?

options.A: High blood pressure and stroke
options.B: Sudden bone fractures
options.C: Malnutrition and anemia
options.D: Rapid hair loss and blindness

explanation: Parasites steal nutrients and blood from the host, which often leads to poor growth and anemia in young ones. You nailed it!

question: Why is getting the community involved so important during an outbreak?

options.A: It ensures that international donors send financial aid instantly
options.B: It eliminates the need for any laboratory testing or clinical staff
options.C: It completely stops the replication cycle of bacteria and viruses
options.D: It builds trust and prevents resistance or hiding of sick family members

explanation: When people trust nurses and understand what's going on, they cooperate openly and report sickness early instead of hiding it.

question: A community health nurse sees poor nutrition in a crowded neighborhood with many empty lots. What is a practical step to take?

options.A: Setting up community gardens and urban farming projects on the vacant lots
options.B: Building a large international shipping port in the city center
options.C: Replacing all local food markets with fast-food outlets
options.D: Encouraging residents to travel out of state for grocery shopping

explanation: Spot on, future nurse! Turning empty lots into gardens is a brilliant way to fight nutritional deserts and bring fresh food to the community.

question: Why do dry-heat cooking methods create brown crusts and rich flavors on food?

options.A: They use high temperatures that trigger the Maillard reaction on the food surface.
options.B: They rely on water molecules to break down complex sugars into simple starches.
options.C: They add liquid fats that caramelize quickly when exposed to steam.
options.D: They remove all moisture from the food interior before cooking begins.

explanation: When high dry heat hits proteins and sugars on the surface, it causes the famous Maillard reaction—giving us that wonderful roasted aroma and golden crust.

question: What is the main internal chip that powers a microcomputer?

options.A: A massive cooling tower
options.B: A microprocessor
options.C: A dual mainframe processor
options.D: An analog wave converter

explanation: Spot on! A tiny microprocessor chip is the brain inside every microcomputer, doing all the heavy thinking.
